sections.name: File setup, tabs
sections.title: Imports and tab names
sections.what: Loads the layout pieces, icons, theme, shared UI parts and the API client. Also lists the three tab names: Medicine, Water and Meals.
sections.why: The API client is the shared way the app talks to the server.

sections.name: MedicineItem
sections.title: Shape of a medicine reminder
sections.what: Describes what a medicine reminder looks like when it arrives from the server: name, dose, times, days and meal timing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Writing the shape down makes the screen code easier to read.
sections.watch_out: This shape is only a label. Nothing checks incoming data against it, so a field the server renames fails quietly.

sections.name: WaterItem
sections.title: Shape of a water reminder
sections.what: Describes the water settings: daily goal, reminder gap, active hours and glass size.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Same as the medicine shape: nothing checks the data on arrival, so a mismatch fails silently.

sections.name: MealItem
sections.title: Shape of a meal reminder
sections.what: Describes one meal reminder: meal type, scheduled time, dietary notes and whether it is active.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The scheduled time is plain text, not a date, so it is shown exactly as the server sends it.

sections.name: ReminderLogItem
sections.title: Shape of a reminder response
sections.what: Describes one saved response: which reminder it belongs to, its type, when it was due, and the user's answer.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These records let the screen show what was already done.
sections.watch_out: Matching is done by reminder ID, so a reminder with several doses in one day shows only its first response.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Loading data and logging responses
sections.what: Holds the screen's data and loading state. It fetches active reminders from the server, sends a taken, skipped or snoozed answer for a reminder, and works out today's water total and percent.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the comments. One shared fetch keeps all three tabs in step.
sections.watch_out: If the fetch fails, the lists are empty and the screen shows its empty messages. A network problem then looks like no reminders are set.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Screen header and tab switcher
sections.what: Draws the Reminders heading, the three tab buttons, and a scrolling area with pull to refresh and a loading spinner.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Pull to refresh lets the user update the list on demand.
sections.watch_out: The loading spinner hides while a pull to refresh is running, so the user sees only the refresh indicator.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Medicine tab cards
sections.what: Draws one card per medicine with its name, dose, meal timing, times, a status badge, and buttons to mark it taken or snooze it. Once taken, the snooze button goes and the mark button is disabled.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Buttons are disabled while a request is running to stop double taps.
sections.watch_out: The status comes from the first matching response, so a later response for the same reminder may not appear.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Water tab summary and log button
sections.what: Shows the water total against the goal, with a progress bar and percent. A button logs one glass. If there is no water goal, it shows No water goal set instead.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The total is a simple count of glasses.
sections.watch_out: The log button has no upper limit. The total can pass the goal while the bar stops at full.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 5)
sections.title: Meal tab cards
sections.what: Draws one card per meal with its name, scheduled time, any dietary notes, an Eaten or Upcoming badge, and a Mark Eaten button.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It mirrors the medicine card for consistency.
sections.watch_out: The meal name is built by keeping the first letter and lowercasing the rest. This assumes the server sends upper case words such as BREAKFAST.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 6)
sections.title: Card and water layout styles
sections.what: Sets sizes and colors for the tabs, cards, medicine icon, text, water circle, progress bar and the action button row.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are visual settings only.
sections.watch_out: The water circle has a fixed size, which may not suit very small or very large screens.

sections.name: RemindersScreen (part 7)
sections.title: Remaining styles and loading area
sections.what: Finishes the spacing for the action row and sets the centered area used for the loading spinner.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are visual settings only.

summary: The Reminders screen, where the user sees medicine, water and meal reminders from the server and marks each one as taken, skipped or snoozed.
purpose: Lets the user track daily medicines, water and meals, and builds a record of what they actually did.
why: The screen reads live reminders from the server so the user can log what they did. Reason for the three tabs is shown by their labels.
how: On open, the screen asks the server for active reminders and stores the medicines, water goal, meals and past responses. When the user taps a button, the screen sends that response to the server and then reloads the list. The water total is worked out by counting taken water logs and multiplying by the glass size.
inputs: The server's active reminders response, taps on tabs and action buttons, and pull to refresh.
outputs: Visible lists and water progress. Each tap sends a response to the server, which stores it.
risks: A failed request looks the same as having no reminders, because the error is only written to the console. Only the first log for each reminder is shown. Default water settings (250 ml glass, 2500 ml goal) are used silently when the settings are missing.
debug: If lists are empty, check the server response shape and the console message from the fetch. If a mark button does nothing, check the response value sent to the log address. If the water total is wrong, check the water settings and the number of water logs.
